messages:
jordan: Heads-up — noticed a recurring mismatch between staging marketplace usage webhooks and our entitlement snapshots. looks like heartbeats from the partner are sometimes arriving ~5–12 minutes late and we lose the ephemeral entitlement window. :frowning:
sasha: Ugh. Is this the same symptom as the 'zero-usage' gaps from last quarter or different? any logs? :eyes:
jordan: Different timing and pattern. last quarter was duplicate ids; this looks like late arrivals only. quick paste of a failing webhook payload we saw:
```json
{"partner_id":"ACME-42","timestamp":"2026-03-15T18:42:03Z","usage_units":12,"heartbeat_seq":77,"claim_id":"c-9a1b"}
```
jordan: In the staging ledger the claim_id appears after the entitlement snapshot TTL, so it never increments the entitlement and downstream billing shows zero usage.
rajesh: Do we have the partner's event ingestion pipeline ack/window tuned for staging? IIRC production kept a 15min grace window, staging had 2min to keep costs down.
olivia_acme: sorry — we've been throttling staging sends on our side to avoid overload. we pushed a retry policy change yesterday that increased backoff, which probably caused the 5–12 minute gap. sending a fix now to reduce backoff for heartbeat events.
sasha: Ok — two-track suggestion:
1) Temporarily widen staging entitlement TTL to 20m so late arrivals get applied (short term)
2) Add a dedupe+late-arrival handler that can accept events within a configured grace window and mark them for backfill (longer term)
jordan: Agree. also can we log a diagnostic tag for any webhook where receipt_ts - payload.timestamp > 2m so we can graph late arrival distribution? would help decide TTL.
rajesh: I'll add an ingestion metric: `partner_webhook_lag_ms` with labels partner_id and claim_id. Also will emit a countermeter when we drop because of TTL boundary. PR in a bit.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: branch=ingest/lag-metrics, env=staging, expected 3m
jordan: Nice. olivia_acme — once your retry change lands, can you ping here and include a sample of the changed headers so we can correlate? specifically we need any x-retry-count / x-backoff-delay.
olivia_acme: will do. ETA ~10m. thanks for the graceful TTL suggestion.
sasha: After we widen TTL in staging, please run this check to simulate late arrival handling:

```bash
# replay a webhook 10 minutes late
curl -X POST https://staging-ingest.redwood.example/marketplace/webhook \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"partner_id":"ACME-42","timestamp":"2026-03-15T18:32:00Z","usage_units":5,"heartbeat_seq":70,"claim_id":"c-test"}'
```
rajesh: I'll coordinate the staging TTL change and add the lag metric. also adding an alert: if >1% of partner events hit >5m lag for 3 consecutive 5m windows, page the oncall and ping partnerships.
jordan: Perfect. let's also add a short runbook note: "if partner heartbeats delayed -> widen staging TTL -> require partner retry/backoff change -> schedule backfill for missing claims". sasha can you add that to partnerships runbook? :memo:
sasha: Yep, adding now.
jordan: thanks — tagging this as action items: rajesh (ingest metric + TTL tweak), sasha (runbook + alerts), olivia_acme (retry policy change and header samples). reconvene in this thread after the replay test. :thumbsup:
